I've been farming this land for 50 years, so let me think through this season the same way I always do — start from what worked last year and adjust a little.

I have 25.1 mu, all in wheat-maize rotation like most folks around Quzhou. That's a fair size — bigger than my neighbor Old Wang but smaller than the families who rent extra land. With just me and my wife in the household, I'll need to hire some help at wheat harvest and maize planting time, those two weeks are too much for us alone.

**Winter wheat (already in ground from last October, will harvest June):**
Last fall I planted Jimai 22 again — it's done well for me five years running, neighbors all use it too. I sowed it after the maize came off in early October, used the rotary tiller from the village service. For base fertilizer I put down compound fertilizer 15-15-15, about 50 kg per mu before sowing. That gives roughly 7.5 kg each of N, P, K per mu in the base.

Now in spring (jointing stage, around now), I'll topdress urea — about 20 kg per mu, that's around 9 kg of N. So total N comes to about 17 kg per mu. I know the agriculture station tells us to use less, but I'd rather put a little extra than watch the wheat turn yellow. A bad wheat harvest costs me far more than the extra bag of urea.

Irrigation: I'll water at jointing (now), then again at heading if it's dry — well water is reliable but the electricity costs add up. Usually 2 times in spring, plus the winter irrigation I already did in December. So 3 total.

Pesticide: spray once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading time, sometimes twice if pests are bad. Plan for 2.

**Summer maize (plant in June right after wheat harvest):**
I'll use Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid — Old Liu down the road got 650 kg/mu last year with it. No-till planter from the cooperative, drill straight into the wheat stubble. Saves time and the straw mulch helps with moisture.

Base fertilizer with the planter: compound 15-15-15, about 40 kg/mu. Then topdress urea at big trumpet stage — 25 kg/mu of urea, about 11 kg N. Total N around 17 kg per mu.

Maize needs water at the trumpet and tasseling stage — usually 2 irrigations from the well if rain is short. Spray once for corn borer, maybe a second time if armyworm shows up.

Last year I got about 480 kg/mu wheat and 580 kg/mu maize. I'll aim for similar this year.
